name: UISizeConstraint
simple: A UISizeConstraint sets a smallest and biggest size, in pixels, for its parent UI object. If you size things with Scale, they can get tiny on phones or huge on big monitors; this keeps them in a sensible range.
analogy: It's like a rule for a growing plant pot: 'never smaller than this, never bigger than that.' The plant can grow, but only so much.
whenToUse: Stopping a Scale-sized menu from becoming giant on a TV
Making sure a button never gets too tiny to tap on a phone
Letting a grid item span more than one cell (MinSize bigger than CellSize)
where: Put it inside the UI object to limit. Create in Studio or with Instance.new in a LocalScript.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.constraint: A rule that limits something. Here it limits size.
terms.infinity (math.huge): A number bigger than any other. Using it for MaxSize means 'no maximum'.

examples.title: A menu that grows with the screen, within limits
examples.place: LocalScript inside a Frame (in a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
examples.code:
local menu = script.Parent
menu.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.4, 0.5) -- 40% of screen width, 50% of height

local limits = Instance.new("UISizeConstraint")
limits.MinSize = Vector2.new(250, 200) -- never smaller than 250 x 200 pixels
limits.MaxSize = Vector2.new(600, 450) -- never bigger than 600 x 450 pixels
limits.Parent = menu
explain: On a 1000x600 screen, Scale gives 400x300 pixels: inside the limits, so nothing changes.
On a small 500x400 phone, Scale would give 200x200, but MinSize bumps it up to 250x200.
On a huge 2560x1440 monitor, Scale would give 1024x720, but MaxSize caps it at 600x450.

gotchas: MinSize must be smaller than or equal to MaxSize on both X and Y.
The constraint beats list and grid layouts: it decides the final min and max size.
Sizes are in pixels, so think about both tiny phones and big screens.

UISizeConstraint.MaxSize.simple: The biggest the parent can be, in pixels (X = width, Y = height). Must be at least as big as MinSize. Use math.huge for 'no limit'.
UISizeConstraint.MaxSize.example:
local limits = script.Parent -- a UISizeConstraint
limits.MaxSize = Vector2.new(500, math.huge) -- at most 500 wide, any height

UISizeConstraint.MinSize.simple: The smallest the parent can be, in pixels (X = width, Y = height). Must be no bigger than MaxSize.
UISizeConstraint.MinSize.example:
local limits = script.Parent
limits.MinSize = Vector2.new(100, 40) -- at least 100 x 40 pixels
